title: Bonus · Sentence ladder 2 (× 3)
summary: Rebuilt 24 Oct: the top of every ladder now comes back at least 3 times (if…, that…, comparisons, questions), every new word is used 3+ times, and it is about 50% longer. Latin read from IPA (v as v), free voices.
pairs: He walks slowly, but I walk fast.
Ille lentē ambulat, sed ego celeriter.
Who walks faster? I do, because my son is three years old.
Quis celerius ambulat? Ego, quia fīlius trēs annōs nātus est.
If my son wants to play, we walk slowly.
Sī fīlius lūdere vult, lentē ambulāmus.
My son says that he is three years old, not small!
Fīlius dīcit sē trēs annōs nātum esse, nōn parvum!
Why did you think so? Because I knew nothing.
Cūr ita putābās? Quia nihil sciēbam.
Now Latin is easier than I thought.
Nunc lingua Latīna facilior est quam putābam.
My wife thought that Latin was easy.
Uxor mea putābat linguam Latīnam facilem esse.
I don't know what to do.
This morning I don't know what to do, that is, I have to do many things.
Hodiē māne nesciō quid faciam, id est, multa facere dēbeō.
If I don't know, my wife knows.
I understand that I have to do many things.
What shall I do? I have to do many things.
Tomorrow I will meet the client.
The meeting was long, but good.
Yesterday I met the client; the meeting was long, but good.
Herī clientem convēnī; conventus longus erat, sed bonus.
When will you meet the client again? Tomorrow.
If I have a good meeting, I am happy.
Sī conventum bonum habeō, laetus sum.
I think that the meeting with the client was good.
Putō conventum cum cliente bonum fuisse.
He said that he was tired.
She says that she is happy.
I am happy, because I am learning.
Why are you happy? Because I am learning, like a boy at school.
Cūr laetus es? Quia ut puer in lūdō discō.
My wife says that I am happy, because I am learning.
Uxor mea dīcit mē laetum esse, quia discō.
If I learn every day, I am happy; if I learn nothing, sad.
Sī cotīdiē discō, laetus sum; sī nihil discō, trīstis.
Now I can speak Latin a little.
Do you speak Latin? A little; I speak English better.
Loquerisne Latīnē? Paulum; linguā Anglicā melius loquor.
If I speak slowly, you understand well.
My wife says that I can now speak Latin a little.
Uxor mea dīcit mē nunc paulum Latīnē loquī posse.
Grātiās tibi agō quod mē adiūvistī.
Thank you for helping my son.
Grātiās tibi agō quod fīlium meum adiūvistī.
Who helped you, Patrick? My wife.
Quis tē adiūvit, Patricī? Uxor mea.
If you help me again, I will help you.
Sī mē iterum adiuvābis, tē adiuvābō.
I know that you helped my son.
When I get home, I will eat.
When I got home, I ate.
When I got home, I ate dinner with my family.
Cum domum vēnissem, cum familiā meā cēnam ēdī.
Why must you go home? So that I can eat dinner with my daughters.
Cūr domum īre dēbēs? Ut cum fīliābus meīs cēnam edam.
If I get home fast, I will play with my little son.
Sī domum celeriter vēnerō, cum fīliō parvō lūdam.
My wife knows that I ate dinner with the family.
Uxor mea scit mē cum familiā cēnam ēdisse.
I read a book every day.
Which book do you read after dinner? A Latin book.
Post cēnam quem librum legis? Librum Latīnum.
I am happy, because my family is here.
Laetus sum, quia familia mea adest.
If my family is here, I am happy.
Sī familia mea adest, laetus sum.
My wife says that I am happy, because the family is here.
Uxor mea dīcit mē laetum esse, quia familia adest.
Why do your body and legs hurt? Because I walked a lot.
Cūr corpus et crūra dolent? Quia multum ambulāvī.
Today my head and legs hurt less than yesterday.
Hodiē caput et crūra minus dolent quam herī.
If my head and body hurt, I stay at home and sleep well.
Sī caput et corpus dolent, domī maneō et bene dormiō.
My wife thinks that I am sad, because my head hurts.
Uxor mea putat mē trīstem esse, quia caput dolet.
If it rains, we stay at home.
If you want, we can walk.
Do you want to walk together after dinner? I do, but it's raining.
Vīsne post cēnam ūnā ambulāre? Volō, sed pluit.
My wife is here and says that it isn't raining.
Uxor mea adest et dīcit nōn pluere.
Walking is better than staying at home and sleeping.
Ambulāre melius est quam domī manēre et dormīre.
If it rains, we don't walk together after dinner.
Sī pluit, post cēnam ūnā nōn ambulāmus.
What is the friend's name? He is called Marcus.
Quod nōmen est amīcō? Marcus vocātur.
What are you called? I'm called Patrick, and I live in Australia.
Quōmodo vocāris? Patricius vocor, et in Austrāliā habitō.
Where does Marcus live? In Australia.
If Marcus is here, we speak Latin.
My friend Marcus says that he lives in Australia.
Amīcus meus Marcus dīcit sē in Austrāliā habitāre.
How did you come today? On foot, that is, I walked.
Quōmodo hodiē vēnistī? Pedibus, id est, ambulāvī.
If it rains, I come by car.
Coming on foot is better than sitting in the car.
Pedibus venīre melius est quam in currū sedēre.
My wife says that I came on foot today.
Uxor mea dīcit mē hodiē pedibus vēnisse.
Lingua Latīna difficilior est quam Anglica.
I think that English is easier, but less beautiful.
Putō linguam Anglicam faciliōrem esse, sed minus pulchram.
My wife thinks that Latin is more beautiful than English.
Uxor mea putat linguam Latīnam pulchriōrem esse quam Anglicam.
Is English easier? Yes, but less beautiful.
Estne lingua Anglica facilior? Ita, sed minus pulchra.
If Latin is hard, I learn slowly.
Sī lingua Latīna difficilis est, lentē discō.
Why is this road better? Because it is more beautiful.
Cūr haec via melior est? Quia pulchrior est.
If I walk on the road, I am happy; if I sit, tired.
Sī in viā ambulō, laetus sum; sī sedeō, fessus.
When I was a boy, I played.
When I was a boy, I didn't learn Latin.
Cum puer eram, linguam Latīnam nōn discēbam.
What did you learn at school?
I want to learn two thousand words.
My goal is two thousand words.
Mēta mea est duo mīlia verbōrum.
Why do you want to learn two thousand words? So that I can speak better.
Cūr duo mīlia verbōrum discere vīs? Ut melius loquar.
My daughters think that my goal is good.
Fīliae meae putant mētam meam bonam esse.
If I learn two thousand words, I speak better.
Sī duo mīlia verbōrum discō, melius loquor.
My goal is less easy than I thought, but don't worry!
Mēta mea minus facilis est quam putābam, sed nōlī cūrāre!
It's hard, but I will try.
Why couldn't you? Because it was hard.
Cūr nōn potuistī? Quia difficile erat.
If it's hard, I try again.
My wife says that I tried.
Uxor mea dīcit mē cōnātum esse.
When will you see me? On Sunday, that is, tomorrow.
Quandō mē vidēbis? Diē Dominicō, id est, crās.
On Sunday morning let's go for a walk together with the family.
Diē Dominicō māne ūnā cum familiā ambulātum eāmus.
When will we go for a walk? On Sunday morning, with the family.
Quandō ambulātum ībimus? Diē Dominicō māne, cum familiā.
If it rains on Sunday, we will not go for a walk.
Sī Diē Dominicō pluet, ambulātum nōn ībimus.
My wife wants to go for a walk together on Sunday.
Uxor mea vult Diē Dominicō ūnā ambulātum īre.
Thank you, my friend. Don't worry. Goodbye!
Grātiās tibi agō, amīce. Nōlī cūrāre. Valē!
